is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles gambiae s.l. (specifically An. gambiae s.s.) collected in Uganda and Kenya (e.g., page 1, 8).

reports_target_markers.evidence: Genotypes target resistance markers including Vgsc L1014S (Vgsc L995S) and Cyp4j5 L43F (pages 4-6, Table 1, Table 2).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Reports overall allele frequencies and total allele counts across 7 field populations for Cyp4j5 (N=1370 alleles) and Vgsc L1014S (N=1068 alleles) in Table 2, as well as baseline Vgsc L1014S frequency (0.94) in wild Tororo females.

african_field_population.evidence: Field mosquito collections were conducted in multiple African locations: Tororo, Oyam, Apac, Jinja, Nagongera, Kanungu in Uganda, and Busia/Bungoma and Teso in Western Kenya (pages 5, 8, 10).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical candidate-gene GWAS and replication study testing association of candidate SNPs with pyrethroid resistance.

sub_country_location.evidence: Specific sub-country locations and coordinates are reported (e.g., Tororo: 00°40'41.6"N, 34°11'11.6"E; Oyam: 02°14'N 32°23'E; Apac: 01°59'N 32°32'E; Jinja: 00°46'N 34°01'E; Nagongera, Kanungu, Busia/Bungoma, Teso).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Sample collections are specified by year: Tororo (2008, 2013-2014), Apac (2008), Oyam (2008), Jinja (2011), Teso (2012), Western Kenya (2013), Kanungu (2014) (Figure 3, pages 8, 10).

duplicate_risk.evidence: Some replication field sample sets originate from previously published collection series (e.g., Jinja from Mawejje et al. 2013 [ref 65], Nagongera from Kilama et al. 2014 [ref 66], Western Kenya from Ochomo et al. 2014 [ref 38]).

supplement.evidence: Per-population breakdown of sample sizes, allele frequencies, and odds ratios for replication field sites are located in Supplementary Table S4 ('see Table S4 for full results').

assessment.summary: This candidate-gene GWAS identified and validated DNA markers associated with metabolic and target-site pyrethroid resistance in field populations of Anopheles gambiae from Uganda and Kenya. Significant associations were demonstrated for Vgsc L1014S (Vgsc L995S) and Cyp4j5 L43F across multiple field collections exposed to permethrin, deltamethrin, and lambda-cyhalothrin.
